chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a man against whom two witnesses testified that he had committed theft. So his hand was cut. But then afterwards, the two witnesses came forward with another man and said, 'This is the thief, not the one whose hand you cut — we only confused that one with this one.' So he (peace be upon him) ruled against them both, imposing upon them both a fine of half the blood-money (diya), and did not allow their testimony against the other man.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful — honorific title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.الدِّيَة: Diya — blood-money or financial compensation prescribed by Islamic law for bodily harm or death
key_terms.شَهَادَة: Shahada (in judicial context) — formal legal testimony given before a judge
key_terms.غَرَّمَ: Gharrama — to impose a financial penalty on someone for harm they caused

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when witnesses falsely testify leading to wrongful amputation? What compensation is owed?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates a judicial case from the practice of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS) as reported by Imam al-Baqir (AS). Two witnesses testified that a man had stolen, leading to the amputation of his hand under the Islamic hadd punishment. Later they returned admitting they had confused the man with the actual thief. Imam Ali ruled that each witness must pay half the diya for the wrongful amputation caused by their mistaken testimony, and that their credibility as witnesses was disqualified for the subsequent case against the real thief. This ruling establishes the financial liability of witnesses for harms caused by erroneous testimony and the principle that false witnesses lose their standing to testify in related matters.
